evidence: Abstract: alignment probe predicts export across 36 configurations at Spearman ρ=+0.68; closed-form activation edit works at layer 7 of 28 and is indistinguishable from base by layer 14.
§4.1 Table 2: seven conditions split perfectly by whether the recipe computed LM cross-entropy; G-inject reaches 0.600 on 4-way matching but 0.125 (chance) on first-sub-word production.

§3.3/Appendix A Table 7: contrasts found on g0 and confirmed on held-out groups at 6/6; confirmation ratios show effects shrink up to 2.4× out of sample, and magnitudes are quoted from the confirmation column.
§5.2 Table 4: activation-arm identity peaks 0.584 at layer 7 and falls to 0.040 at layer 14 (within ±0.008 of final-norm baseline); weight arm peaks 0.800–0.808 at layers 10–14.
§5.1: anchoring at the readout drives SAR from 0.583 to 1.000 but export moves −0.07, showing alignment predicts but does not cause export.

§6.1 Table 5: window replicates on Janus-Pro (peak 0.583 vs base 0.052) but is null on Lumina-DiMOO and Omni-Diffusion; word-target instrument check moves nulls to 6.3× and 2.0× their floors, attributing nulls to the visual address not the method.
§7 Table 6: anchoring alone retains 0.680 GenEval (−0.1% relative) while the generative default drops to 0.401 (−41.0%), with damage tied to presence of flow-matching gradient steps.
§8 Limitations: the four-model semantic-format split is observational with encoder type covarying with backbone, scale and generation mechanism; identity lacks human-judgment calibration.
Appendix J: every number is produced by a script in the accompanying code release; training runs single-GPU, idempotent, with generated command lines; code at github.com/Zane-ZYQiu/entry-point-umm.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A multimodal interpretability/model-editing study of unified multimodal models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro, Lumina-DiMOO, Omni-Diffusion) with substantial language methodology: LM cross-entropy training, context-free name-production probes scored via LM forward passes, and ROME/MEMIT-style edits in the LLM backbone, so it is in scope rather than capped as pure CV or diffusion. Preference fit is moderate: strong matches to interpretability (activation patching, probing, attention-vs-MLP substrate, entry-point localization) and multimodal AI, but no overlap with the highest-weight preferences (reasoning, agents, Japanese LLM, alignment). Novelty is solid: contamination-free single-direction binding, matching-vs-production dissociation, entry-point depth window, and closed-form activation edit are new framings, though built on DreamBooth/Textual-Inversion, ROME/MEMIT, and REPA. Rigor is exceptional: pre-specified arbiter column (§3.2), discovery/confirmation protocol with held-out groups and retracted contrasts (§3.3, Appendix A), derangement/magnitude/placebo controls (Table 17), instrument checks, second encoder agreement r=0.997, and honest nulls (G→U rate asymmetry left unresolved in §4.1; two architecture nulls instrument-verified via word-target check, Table 15). Evidence is strong with bootstraps and cross-architecture replication, though the semantic-format rule rests on a four-model observational series where encoder type covaries with scale and mechanism (§8 Limitation ii), and identity uses automatic encoders rather than human judgment. Generalizability is decent but bounded by the observational architecture comparison and eight-concept groups. Reproducibility claims are strong: public code, scripted regeneration of every table (Appendix J).

papers.summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) are motivated by the hope that understanding and generation reinforce each other but controlled ablations repeatedly find that adding a generation objective leaves understanding flat. Joint-training studies cannot settle the disagreement: with overlapping supervision, a gain cannot be attributed to the architecture rather than the data. To further investigate the relationship between the two directions in UMMs, we separate them by construction. A novel visual ent
papers.summary_zh: 統一多模態模型（UMM）標榜理解與生成能互相強化，但控制變因的消融實驗卻一再顯示加入生成目標對理解幫助有限。本文指出聯合訓練的證據無法把增益歸因於架構而非資料，因此設計一套「零污染」協定：將新穎視覺實體（3D 資產搭配經篩選的虛構詞）僅透過單一任務方向寫入凍結模型，再量測未訓練方向的表現。結果顯示通道雙向皆存在，但性質不同：生成訓練只讓模型能在候選中配對名稱，理解訓練則讓模型能主動產出名稱並畫出概念。核心發現是「入口位置」決定跨任務可用性：對齊探針可預測 36 種設定的輸出表現（Spearman ρ=+0.68），但把它推到頂點並無幫助；閉式激活編輯在第 7 層（共 28 層）有效、第 14 層起與基礎模型無異，權重版則於第 10–14 層達峰。跨四種架構顯示，只有理解路徑採語意視覺編碼器（BAGEL、Janus-Pro）才出現有效窗口，採 VQ 碼本的模型則失敗，證明統一權重並不足夠，兩方向須在入口處以共同語意格式表示概念。據此提出的層中段語意錨定法完全不計算生成梯度，即可習得 56 個概念，僅損失 0.1% 的一般文生圖能力，遠低於標準生成路線的 41%。限制包括以層數近似下游計算量、架構比較屬觀察性研究，以及以自動編碼器評估身分準確度。

evidence: Section 5.1: evaluates on 36 datasets (4 transductive, 12 IndE, 20 FullInd) against 17 baselines including ULTRA, MOTIF, KICGPT, MKGL, and KRLM, using Qwen2.5-1.5b backbone on 4 A100 40GB GPUs

Table 1 / Tables 8-9 (Appendix J.1): SIRLM_SFT reaches 0.599 MRR / 0.749 Hit10 averaged over 12 IndE datasets vs KRLM 0.578/0.737, with per-dataset tables showing negative gains on MTDEA2-org Hit10 (-3.74%) and minimal gain on WN18RR v1 (+0.38%)
Table 10 (Appendix J.2): ablations w/o SRM and w/o RCMP drop FB15k237 MRR from 0.408 to 0.358 and 0.352 respectively, supporting each module's contribution
Appendix E, Propositions 1-2 with proofs: WL-test-based argument that SRM improves structural alignment and RCMP strictly refines SIL expressiveness, though resting on stated assumptions (B1-B4)
Appendix G, Table 4: efficiency comparison showing SIRLM_PT at 2.04 avg TFLOPs and 27.58 GB/GPU vs KRLM 3.34 TFLOPs and 36.12 GB/GPU in pre-training
Section 5.5, Table 2 and Figure 9 (Appendix J.3): backbone study across Qwen2.5-0.5b/1.5b/7b and Llama-2-7b showing 0.5b lags (e.g., CoDEx-M MRR 0.351 vs 0.369)

Reproducibility statement + Appendices A, F, H, I: anonymous GitHub code link, training pseudocode (Algorithm 1), instruction schema, dataset statistics (Table 5), and full hyperparameter tables (Tables 6-7), though Table 6 is mislabeled 'Hyperperameters of KRLM'

Appendix K and Figure 8: authors acknowledge quadratic computational upper bound for large KGs and degraded performance on sparse KGs due to limited rule availability; no statistical significance testing appears anywhere in Section 5 or appendices
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM-methodology paper: internalizes KG structural knowledge into a Qwen2.5-1.5B backbone via a structural-token KG tokenizer, a memory-augmented in-context attention block (SRM), rule-constrained message propagation (RCMP), and SFT/GRPO training, directly matching high-weight preferences (LLM, reasoning/faithfulness, knowledge grounding, in-context learning, LoRA/SFT/GRPO training). Extensive evaluation on 36 datasets against 17 baselines with per-component ablations, backbone study, complexity comparison, and WL-test expressiveness proofs is above average rigor, but gains are modest on several benchmarks (e.g., WN18RR v1 +0.38%, MTDEA2-org Hit10 -3.74%), no seed variance or significance testing is reported, the 'Avg. gain' metric cherry-favors the best of four training modes, and copy-paste artifacts (Table 6 labeled 'Hyperperameters of KRLM', SILRM/SIRLM inconsistency) and a garbled Appendix D definition of semantic drift magnitude slightly undercut polish. Novelty is incremental over the ULTRA/MOTIF structural-invariance line and the authors' own KRLM, mainly adding the rule-generation feedback loop and faithfulness reward. Code, pseudocode, dataset partitions, and hyperparameters are provided, supporting decent reproducibility, though the repo is only claimed, not verifiable from the text.

primary_link.title: Structure-Internalized Rule Language Model for Faithful Knowledge Graph Reasoning

papers.summary: Knowledge Graph Reasoning (KGR) aims to discover latent facts by leveraging the structural evidence available in KGs, posing a challenge to the structural semantic understanding capability of KGR models. Recent studies have demonstrated that Large Language Models (LLMs) can achieve remarkable progress on KGR tasks via flexible in-context learning. However, the inherent representation inconsistency between KG structural context and LLM parametric knowledge remains inadequately addressed. This lim
papers.summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）雖在知識圖譜推理（KGR）上表現亮眼，但其參數知識與圖譜結構語意之間的表示不一致，使模型傾向依預訓練語意偏好挑選證據，生成看似合理卻難以在圖譜上落地的推理邏輯，作者稱之為「推理證據感知漂移」。為此，本文提出結構內化規則語言模型 SIRLM，核心包括三項組件：其一，基於結構不變性學習（SIL）的 KG tokenizer，透過關係圖與 NBFNet 將實體與關係編碼為通用結構 token，使 LLM 在匿名化情境下仍能感知圖譜證據；其二，配備結構關係記憶（SRM）的規則產生器 SIRG，在注意力層注入結構記憶以對齊參數知識與結構脈絡，並以自迴歸方式生成可執行的結構規則；其三，以規則約束訊息傳播（RCMP）為基礎的神經符號推理器，將生成規則轉為初始化訊號並回饋忠實性評分，形成閉環最佳化。SIRLM 可無縫整合 SFT 與 GRPO 等標準訓練範式。在 36 個資料集（4 個直推式、12 個歸納實體、20 個全歸納）對抗 17 個先進方法，四種訓練模式皆具優勢，全歸納場景平均增益逾 10%。消融實驗證實 SRM 與 RCMP 至關重要，且於 0.5B 至 7B 骨幹皆表現穩定。限制為圖譜處理的計算複雜度以實體數衡量上界偏高，以及稀疏圖譜因規則證據不足而表現受限；作者規劃引入查詢驅動證擊圖與軟規則機制改善。
papers.title: Structure-Internalized Rule Language Model for Faithful Knowledge Graph Reasoning

links.title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth

evidence: Sec. 3.4: seven architectures (TRM-style, UT/URM, FPRM, EqR, DEQ, Neural GPU, SE-RRM) re-implemented at matched size and budget, trained on identical data files, protocol, seeds; Huginn-3.5B measured via forward hooks only

Sec. 5.4 / Fig. 3: removing the fixed-point objective flips regime settle→drift (λ_max −0.06→+0.10) and destroys Sudoku extrapolation 0.34→0.03; adding it to the generic recurrence converts carry 0.12→0.88 with damage 0.91→0

Sec. 5.4: among 164 competent original-ladder runs, none of the 17 settling runs loses more than 0.004 EM to depth while 30% marginal and 22% drifting lose more than 0.1 (p=1e-3); pooled conversion not cluster-significant
Sec. 3.3: Sudoku scored with a validity oracle; uniquely-solvable fraction 1.00/0.91/0.50/0.06/0.00 per tier; valid/reference gap 5.5× on unseen-hard (0.34 vs 0.062)

Sec. 7.1 / App. H: rank-16 LoRA on Huginn-3.5B recurrent core with label-free latent anchor restores digit copying 0.00→1.00±0.00 at r=128 (10/10 seeds) and letter repetition 0.00→0.51±0.13; conversion never appears

App. K: strictly-beyond-horizon carry conversion did not replicate (16-round tier exceeds 0.5 on 1/25 seeds), so no beyond-horizon conversion claim is made; dose-response shows depth-safety switching on at the settling crossing
App. E: estimator scope — only top-8 finite-time Lyapunov exponents, PCA-reduced trajectories, regime thresholds not load-bearing, AUC 0.846 for Lyapunov spread vs 0.390 for |λ_max| alone
Sec. 8 (Limitations): synthetic generators from one symmetry orbit, small scale, repair operation-family-scoped to one checkpoint, regime not claimed as sole mediator
App. R: anonymized code supplement with generators, checksummed materialized splits, exact seeds, per-run logs, and regeneration scripts; 'pre-committed' commits are not timestamped by a third party
llm_evaluation.rationale: A dynamical-systems study of when test-time depth helps recurrent reasoners, directly relevant to the Reasoning & CoT preference (test-time compute, overthinking, latent chain-of-thought) with partial LLM relevance via measurement and LoRA repair of Huginn-3.5B and probes of open 7B reasoners (Sec. 7), though the core experiments are tiny models on synthetic algorithmic ladders rather than LLMs, capping preference fit. Novelty is solid: measuring the trained operator's finite-time regime (settling/marginal/drift), a depth-safety proposition, and a causal one-term fixed-point objective switch are a genuine delta over Anil et al. path-independence, DEQ stabilization, and Labovich's theory (Sec. 2). Rigor is unusually high: pre-committed protocols, byte-shared splits, matched-budget re-implementations of seven architectures, three-to-20 seeds, cluster bootstrap, dose-response sweeps, and honest estimator-scope caveats (App. E). Evidence is strong for depth-safety (0/17 settling runs lose >0.004 EM vs 30%/22% for marginal/drift, p=1e-3, Sec. 5.4) and the Huginn repair (digit copying 0.00→1.00±0.00, 10 seeds, App. H), but weaker for conversion: pooled conversion is not cluster-significant, Sudoku's 0.34 headline rests partly on a validity oracle with only 0.062 reference match (Sec. 3.3), and strictly-beyond-horizon carry conversion failed to replicate (App. K) — all transparently reported. Generalizability is limited by synthetic generators, small scale, and a single-checkpoint operation-family-scoped repair (Sec. 8). Reproducibility is strong: anonymized supplement with checksummed splits, per-run logs, and regeneration scripts (App. R), with the caveat that 'pre-committed' commits are not third-party timestamped.

primary_link.title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth

papers.summary: Recurrent-depth reasoners aim to solve harder problems by iterating their update longer at test time, but additional iterations can improve, preserve, or degrade an answer. We show that a measurable property of the trained operator, its finite-time dynamical regime (estimated as settling, marginal, or drifting), indicates which of these occurs. We give a sufficient condition for depth-safety: once an operator's per-step displacement is small relative to the decoder margin, the decoded answer can
papers.summary_zh: 遞迴深度推理器透過在測試時反覆迭代同一區塊來「想更久」，但增加迭代可能改善、維持或損害答案。本文主張訓練後算子的有限時間動力學狀態（收斂、邊際或漂移）能預測結果，並證明當每步位移相對解碼器邊距夠小時，答案必不因後續迭代而改變，為深度安全性提供充分條件。實驗涵蓋受控遞迴配方 CoRe 的逐一消融與七種重實作架構，皆在固定資料（每難度層 800 筆、無增廣）下以同一協定訓練。結果顯示收斂型算子不會因加深而退化，部分任務更能將深度轉換為對更難實例的準確率（Sudoku 由 0.19 升至 0.34）；邊際與漂移型則停滯、崩潰或衰減，且何種架構收斂依任務而異。終端不動點目標是因果槓桿：移除它使收斂轉為漂移並摧毀增益；僅將其加入通用遞迴，即可在進位加法上得到深度安全的外推（0.12→0.88）。作者提出四項行為準則與四種可量測的失敗模式，並以頻譜異向性區分「收斂成演算法」與「僅僅收斂」。對 Huginn-3.5B 的量測將其歸入非收斂家族，答案凍結屬於猜測凍結；一套不需標籤的潛在錨定 LoRA 修補恢復了深度安全性（數字複製 0.00→1.00）但不產生深度轉換。限制包括合成資料產生器、模型規模小，以及中介機制尚未完全釐清。
papers.title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth

links.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration

evidence: Abstract: 'TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation'; implementation claimed at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

Section 5.1 (Experimental Setup): 'All experiments run on NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs'; 'Throughput evaluation uses batch size 8, three warmup iterations, and five timed iterations'; baselines include dense FP16, One (uniform INT8), FlashAttention, MInference, FlexPrefill, and SageAttention.

Section 5.3 / Table 2: 'At 4k tokens, SpTrans75 reaches 31.80 K tokens/s, compared with 14.33 K tokens/s for FlashAttention and 29.80 K tokens/s for One', with timings including quantization, scale restoration, routing, memory staging, and scheduling costs.

Table 1 (Section 5.2): dataset 3 at 16k shows SpTrans25/50/75 at 21.04/20.53/21.65 vs FP16 6.72 and One 4.45; Appendix E confirms the same anomaly on Qwen2-7B (50.6/49.7/52.0 vs FP16 16.39) and Qwen2.5-7B, labeled only a 'consistent layout-task interaction' without mechanistic explanation.
Section 5.4 / Table 3: mean absolute output deviation from Torch FP16 increases with INT8 coverage (e.g., at 8k: 6.84e-5 at 0% to 6.84e-3 at 25%), described as a 'practical numerical-control knob'.

Limitations: 'TileMix targets forward inference during long-context prefill'; 'The current implementation instantiates tile-group routing with FP16 and INT8 Tensor Core paths on NVIDIA A100 GPUs'; 'Static routing templates provide deterministic policy construction'.

Appendix C (Quantization Configuration): 'BLK_Q = 128, BLK_K = 64' with signed symmetric absmax INT8 quantization, one scale per block per head; Appendix D details quantize-once vs fused on-the-fly operand modes and memory accounting (Table 5).

Appendix B: evaluated routing templates are 'statically constructed and do not use benchmark outputs for policy selection'; coverage percentages denote legal score-tile-group INT8 coverage, not FLOP fraction.

Appendix G (Tables 19-22): FP16-vs-FP32 accumulation controls show 'routing layout and INT8 coverage produce much larger numerical effects than accumulation precision', with larger-model checks on LLaMA 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 14B; Table 23 reports heavy-hitter INT8 exposure (SpTrans25 routes ~8.5% of high-importance mass to INT8).
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM systems paper on long-context inference acceleration that aligns well with high-weight preferences (LLMs, inference/serving, efficiency, transformer attention); it is methodology work, not a domain application. The kernel contribution (tile-group FP16/INT8 precision routing inside a fused dense FlashAttention-style kernel with packed bitmasks and a shared online-softmax state) is a genuine but incremental kernel-design abstraction building on SageAttention, FlashAttention, and quantized-attention lines, with static layouts borrowed from sparse-attention patterns. Evaluation is broad: LongEval and LV-Eval (11 datasets, 16k-64k) across LLaMA 3.2 3B, Qwen2-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Vicuna-7B, prefill throughput on A100 with matched baselines (FlashAttention, One/uniform INT8, MInference, FlexPrefill, SageAttention), coverage/layout ablations, and numerical controls (FP32 accumulation, layer-wise, larger models). Key weaknesses: a >3x-over-FP16 anomaly (dataset 3 at 16k) is reported but not explained, no significance testing, TOPS is a synthetic metric, throughput measured only to 8k tokens, A100/FP16-INT8/prefill-only scope, and the INT8 KV-cache decode interface is described but not evaluated. Reproducibility is strong given code availability, explicit quantization configuration, storage layouts, and timing protocol.

primary_link.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration

papers.summary: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile group
papers.summary_zh: 長上下文 LLM 推論的 prefill 階段因密集自注意力而產生 O(L²) 的計算量與記憶體流量，現有方法不是採用均一低精度路徑，就是挑選部分 token 互動，鮮少在融合密集注意力內部對硬體對齊的分數 tile 進行空間精度路由。本文提出 TileMix，一個以 tile 為中心的精度路由核心：將注意力矩陣切成硬體對齊的分數 tile，把路由決策打包成 64 位元遮罩，於內層迴圈以常數時間的位移與遮罩運算讀取，將各 tile 群派送至 FP16 或 INT8 Tensor Core 路徑，兩條路徑皆更新共用的 online-softmax 狀態。可擴展的精度分組讓每個路由位元掌控多個相鄰 key tile，在長上下文下仍維持硬體對齊的計算 tile 與精簡中繼資料。此方法保留完整的合法 token 連通性、無需訓練，並支援 GQA、變長批次與 INT8 KV 快取。在 LongEval、LV-Eval 與 A100 prefill 基準上，於 LLaMA、Qwen、Vicuna 等模型驗證：相較均一 INT8 可恢復長上下文品質，相較 FP16 提升預填吞吐量（4k token 時 SpTrans75 達 31.8 K tokens/s，FlashAttention 僅 14.33），構成可控的精度—效率前緣。數值分析顯示輸出偏差隨 INT8 覆蓋率上升，可作為實用的控制手段。限制在於僅針對 prefill 前向推論、目前實作綁定 A100 上的 FP16/INT8 路徑，且採靜態路由模板。
papers.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration
papers.title_zh: TileMix：以 Tile 為中心的混合精度注意力，加速 LLM 推論

links.title: aDSL: Agentic 3D Creation via Joint Agent-Program Design

evidence: Section 1 & Section 3.2: training-free multi-agent system with Planner/Coder/Debugger/Critic roles sharing aDSL as the representation for planning, coding, execution, and verification.
Section 4.1, Table 1: aDSL attains CLIP 29.63 / VQA 65.34 / 1.00 success on ShapeNet, best among code-generation baselines (Scene Language 28.35/59.13, ShapeCraft 27.70/57.26).

Section 4.3, Table 4: replacing aDSL with Blender scripts raises refinement rounds 4.25→6.08; removing spatial utilities drops VQA 65.34→63.75; combined removal is worst (28.20 CLIP, 59.25 VQA, 0.97 success).
Section 4.2, Table 3: on Toys4K image-to-shape, aDSL (CLIP 84.42, FID 184.71) trails field-based Trellis (84.88, 108.20) and is best only among code-generation methods.
Section 4.1 Human Evaluation: 38 participants, 20 cases, prefer aDSL 85.39% for prompt alignment and 86.84% for geometric/visual quality vs Scene Language.
Appendix A Implementation Details: Gemini 3 Pro at temperature 1.0, max R=10 rounds, standardized rendering protocol; Section 1 claims code release at github.com/sig-pku/aDSL.
Section 5 Conclusion: limitations include DSL expressiveness bounds, 2D-rendering-based critique prone to perspective ambiguity, and reliance on strong proprietary LLMs.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core contribution is LLM-agent methodology (joint DSL + multi-agent Plan-Execute-Critic design, training-free, memory management, generate-verify-repair), strongly matching the Agents & Tool Use and Code & Programming preferences with an LLM backbone; not a pure CV/domain application. Novelty is moderate: DSL-for-LLM 3D generation exists (AIDL, Scene Language, ShapeCraft), and the incremental step is co-designing the language around agent capabilities with relational spatial operators. Rigor is solid for the area: text-to-shape benchmark (100 instances/200 prompts across ShapeNet/ABO/Objaverse), Toys4K image-to-shape, six baselines, four-component ablations including Blender-script replacement, and a 38-participant human study, though automatic metrics (CLIP/VQAScore) are weak proxies for 3D quality, scale is small, and gains over the strongest code baseline are modest with no significance testing. Evidence honestly reports that field-based Trellis beats aDSL on image-to-shape CLIP/FID and on ShapeNet VQA, with aDSL best among code-generation methods; ablations (rounds 4.25→6.08 with Blender scripts; VQA 65.34→63.75 without spatial utils; worse combined ablation) directly support the joint-design claim. Generalizability is moderate since the joint-design principle transfers but the DSL is 3D-specific and the system depends on proprietary frontier LLMs (acknowledged as a limitation). Reproducibility is aided by released code, full DSL reference, prompt templates, and protocol details, but the exact benchmark sampling and closed-source backbone limit exact replication.

primary_link.title: aDSL: Agentic 3D Creation via Joint Agent-Program Design

papers.summary: Programmatic representations provide a compelling paradigm for 3D content creation, enabling fine-grained edits, interpretability, and explicit structural control. Yet, agentic workflows that rely on large language models (LLMs) to author 3D programs remain brittle, often failing to translate high-level intent into consistent low-level geometry. We attribute this fragility to a mismatch between existing programmatic interfaces and the reasoning strengths of LLMs, which favor semantic structure a
papers.summary_zh: 本文針對大型語言模型（LLM）代理進行 3D 內容創作時常不可靠的問題：生成結果易偏離使用者意圖，且迭代修正時品質下降。作者認為根本原因在於現有程式化表示法（如 Blender 腳本、CAD 程式碼）與 LLM 推理特性錯配——LLM 擅長語義結構與空間關係推理，卻難以產出精確的底層數值參數。為此，論文聯合設計代理中心領域特定語言（aDSL）與角色分工的多代理系統。aDSL 圍繞表現力、可組合性與空間推理三大原則建構，讓代理以宣告式版面運算子（如「將 A 置於 B 上方」）取代脆弱的絕對座標；代理系統則採行「規劃—執行—批評」迴圈：Planner 分解任務並產出可驗證約束，Coder 合成程式，Critic 依執行紀錄與多視角渲染反覆修復，全程無需訓練。實驗顯示，此方法在文字轉形狀與影像轉形狀任務上超越 Scene Language、ShapeCraft 等基準，執行成功率達 100%，人類評估偏好率約 85%；消融實驗證明空間運算子與迭代修復相輔相成、缺一不可。系統亦支援可關節物件建模、形狀編輯與場景生成等下游應用。限制在於輸出品質受限於 DSL 幾何原語的表現力，驗證仍依賴 2D 渲染而可能有透視歧義，且需要強大的專有 LLM。此研究展示了共享表示法串聯生成、驗證與修復的價值，是代理式 3D 創作的重要進展。
papers.title: aDSL: Agentic 3D Creation via Joint Agent-Program Design
papers.title_zh: aDSL：透過代理與程式聯合設計實現代理式 3D 創作

links.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement

evidence: Abstract: reports 5.6% overall improvement and 19% lower API cost across tasks and models using 8 LLMs including GPT-5, Gemini-2.5 Pro, Claude-4.5 Sonnet.

Section 4.1 (Models): lists GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, o4-mini, o3, o3-mini, Gemini-2.5 Pro, Claude 4.5 Sonnet and states all experiments run three times reporting mean and standard deviation (7 models listed vs '8 LLMs' claimed in abstract).

Findings 1 / Appendix B Table 3: averaged best-over-20-iteration scores — Self feedback 71.0% vs w/o Feedback 66.8%, Correctness/Executor 79.3%, while ICL 62.1%, ACE 64.0%, DC 62.7% trail the no-feedback baseline.

Section 5 Table 1: dual (model+correctness/executor) feedback reaches 76.7% on AIME 2025 vs 70.0% correctness-only and 60.0% model-only with Claude 4.5 Sonnet; DC and SimpleMem within-task selection underperform pure model feedback.
Appendix F.5 Table 4: Cohen's kappa of 0.768 between GPT-5 judge and human annotators on 100 sampled incorrect-to-correct trajectories (76.0% overall agreement).
Appendix B Table 3: GPQA Diamond Correctness/Executor feedback averages 99.52%, a near-ceiling value under oracle binary feedback that warrants scrutiny.
Appendix I Table 5: token vs accuracy analysis, e.g., AIME 2025 correctness feedback 108,734 tokens at 84.6% vs Dynamic CheatSheet 11,233 tokens at 74.7% and no-feedback 106,825 tokens at 74.1%.
Appendix G: on BrowseComp-Plus, self-feedback leads to performance decline relative to no-feedback, an honestly reported negative result for knowledge-heavy, search-dependent tasks.

Appendix L (Limitations): states no model parameters are updated, so gains arise from contextual reuse of experience rather than true learning, and evaluation is limited to math, knowledge, and coding benchmarks.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly on-topic: a training-free test-time study of LLM self-improvement via accumulated experience and feedback (self, executor, correctness), evaluated across math/code/knowledge with GPT-5, o3/o4-mini, Gemini-2.5 Pro, Claude 4.5 Sonnet; squarely matches top-weighted LLM, reasoning, agent/test-time, and code preferences. Novelty is moderate: the core mechanism is Reflexion/Self-Refine-style iterative refinement, and the contribution is a systematic unification and empirical characterization (feedback spectrum, cost/token efficiency, ability-gain correlation, spurious-feedback robustness) rather than a new algorithm. Rigor is decent: 3 runs with std, ablations (dual feedback, DC/SimpleMem within-task selection, 50-iteration extension), and human-validated GPT-5 attribution (Cohen's kappa 0.768, Appendix F.5); however headline gains use 'best accuracy over 20 iterations' (selection-inflated, partially mitigated by SelMV), correctness feedback is an oracle upper bound, and the abstract claims 8 LLMs while §4.1 lists 7 (Figure 3 caption says five). Evidence is internally consistent (Table 3 averages match the reported 66.8/71.0/79.3 figures and token analysis in Appendix I), but the 99.52% average on GPQA Diamond under oracle feedback (Appendix B) is near-ceiling and under-explained, and some claims rest on figures. Generalizability is supported by multi-domain, multi-family results and an honestly reported failure case (self-feedback hurts on BrowseComp-Plus, Appendix G), but is bounded by verifiable-feedback tasks and no weight updates (Appendix L). Reproducibility is middling: public benchmarks and prompt details are provided, but evaluation relies on costly closed APIs (e.g., ~$325/model on EvaLearn) and no code release is stated.

primary_link.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement

papers.summary: Humans continuously learn from experience, whereas conventional large language model (LLM) evaluations ignore the models' ability to improve through inference-time interaction. In this paper, we study how LLMs learn from iterative experience at test time, a setting we refer to as Chain-of-Experience (CoE), where models accumulate experiential traces through iterative interactions with self or environmental feedback to form a continual improvement loop beyond zero-shot inference. We instantiate C
papers.summary_zh: 人類能持續從經驗中學習，但傳統大型語言模型（LLM）評估忽略模型在推論時與環境互動並改進的能力。本文提出「經驗鏈」（Chain-of-Experience, CoE）框架：模型在測試階段與自身或環境反覆互動，累積由回饋構成的經驗軌跡，形成超越零樣本推論的持續改進迴圈。作者系統性探討四種回饋型態——無回饋、模型自我回饋、程式執行回饋與正確性回饋，並在數學（AIME 2025、OmniMath）、編碼（LiveCodeBench、LiveBench）與知識（GPQA Diamond、EvaLearn）等六項基準上，以 GPT-5、Gemini-2.5 Pro、Claude-4.5 Sonnet 等 8 個模型評測。結果顯示：僅憑自我回饋即平均提升 5.6%，並降低 19% 的 API 成本，每個 token 的準確率更高；結合互補回饋通道（如模型與正確性訊號）可得進一步增益；相較 ICL、Dynamic CheatSheet、ACE 等依賴跨任務經驗的方法，CoE 平均高出 7-9 個百分點。研究亦發現基礎能力與改進幅度呈正相關（平均 Pearson 相關係數約 0.5），多數增益在迭代早期出現，且模型面對錯誤或虛假回饋仍具穩健性，選擇性多數決可緩解誤導訊號。限制包括不更新模型參數、評估局限於數學與編碼等領域，對需要外部知識的任務自我回饋反而失效。此研究為測試階段學習提供了統一框架。
papers.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement
papers.title_zh: 經驗鏈：實現大型語言模型的持續改進

links.title: TRUSS: Towards Task-Reliable and User-Safe Automated Agent Skill Generation

evidence: Abstract: 'TRUSS achieves 100.00% precision and recall in vulnerability detection. Repair reduces attack success from 38.71% to 19.35% with GPT 5.5 and from 46.45% to 29.68% with GPT 5.4, with zero attack regression.'
Section 4.2, Table 2: TRUSS 100.00%/100.00%/100.00% vs Static Checker 81.55%/94.05%/87.36% and Intermediate LLM Checker 44.64%/19.05%/26.69% on 168 SkillInject artifacts.
Section 4.3, Table 3: GPT 5.5 eliminates 30 of 60 attacks (ASR 38.71%->19.35%), GPT 5.4 eliminates 26 of 72 (46.45%->29.68%); safe task completion 52.90% vs 23.87% shows a large target-model effect.
Section 4.4, Table 4: Effectiveness 17.11% (No Skills) -> 29.95% (LLM Generator) -> 52.94% (TRUSS); Security 50.80% -> 75.40% -> 100.00% on all 187 SkillGenBench samples.
Section 4.4: 'Their individual contributions require the component ablation reported separately.' — component ablation for RQ3 is not present in the paper.

Section 1 (Contributions) claims 'comprehensive evaluation across 3 agents and 5 models', but Section 4.1 (Target Models and Harnesses) lists only GPT 5.5, GPT 5.4 mini, the Harbor Codex agent, and a Claude Code harness.
Section 3.4.1, Table 1: nine predefined safety properties (P1-P9) with assigned static/runtime evidence phases constitute the safety contract.
No code, artifact release, prompt templates, revision budget, or lambda value is reported anywhere in the paper; all models named (GPT 5.5/5.4) are proprietary.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core in-scope agentic LLM research: automated generation and safety verification of Agent Skills for LLM-based coding agents, touching Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, AI Safety, Red Teaming/Evaluation, and Code. The hybrid static-plus-runtime verification loop (brokered Controllable Execution Environment, provenance-preserving traces, nine predefined safety properties) is a sensible and somewhat novel extension over prior static-only skill checkers (SkillNet, SkillSpector) and execution-guided generation (Skill Set Optimization, EvoSkill), though it largely combines known sandboxing, LLM-judging, and iterative repair ideas. Rigor is mixed: internally consistent arithmetic across Tables 2-4 (e.g., 60/155=38.71% ASR, 99/187=52.94% effectiveness) and ablation of checker stages for RQ1, but perfect 100% detection and 100% Security raise overfitting concerns, the contribution claims '3 agents and 5 models' while Section 4.1 describes only GPT 5.5/5.4 with Codex and a Claude Code harness, no external baselines (e.g., SkillSpector, SkillNet) or component ablation for RQ3 ('reported separately' but absent), and no significance testing or variance reporting. Evidence strength is moderate given detailed counts but entirely self-reported results on the very benchmarks the framework's checks target. Generalizability is limited by benchmark- and model-specific tuning and acknowledged sensitivity to scenario coverage. No code, prompts, revision budget, or lambda value is disclosed, hurting reproducibility.

primary_link.title: TRUSS: Towards Task-Reliable and User-Safe Automated Agent Skill Generation

papers.summary: Agent Skills package reusable natural language procedures with executable resources, enabling software agents to acquire task specific capabilities without model adaptation. Automatically generating such Skills can improve task performance, yet evaluating a candidate solely from its artifact or final task outcome leaves unresolved which actions the equipped agent will perform and which side effects those actions will produce. We present TRUSS, an evidence guided framework for generating function
papers.summary_zh: 代理技能（Agent Skills）封裝可重複使用的自然語言程序與可執行資源，讓軟體代理無需微調模型即能習得特定任務能力；但僅憑成品或最終任務結果評估候選技能，無法確知代理實際會執行哪些動作及產生哪些副作用。本文提出 TRUSS，一個以證據為引導的技能生成框架，同時兼顧功能有效性與安全可靠性。其流程為：生成器產出候選技能套件後，檢查器先對功能主張進行證據檢驗，並依九項預定義安全屬性（如控制完整性、存取邊界、執行完整性）審查成品；通過靜態門檻的候選再由影子代理載入可控制執行環境（CEE），所有工具請求經中介式工具攔截，產生保留來源的執行軌跡；功能失敗與屬性違規會連結回具體技能內容，引導精煉器迭代修訂。實驗結果亮眼：在 168 個 SkillInject 樣本上，漏洞偵測的精確率與召回率均達 100%；修復測試中，GPT 5.5 的攻擊成功率從 38.71% 降至 19.35%，GPT 5.4 從 46.45% 降至 29.68%，且零攻擊回歸；在 187 個 SkillGenBench 任務上，任務有效率從無技能的 17.11% 提升至 52.94%，安全率達 100%。限制在於執行場景覆蓋度與執行者行為仍會影響驗證結果。此框架證明執行證據能揭露靜態檢查遺漏的行為缺陷，為代理技能的安全自動化生成提供可行方案。
papers.title: TRUSS: Towards Task-Reliable and User-Safe Automated Agent Skill Generation
papers.title_zh: TRUSS：邁向任務可靠且使用者安全的自動化代理技能生成

links.title: When Writing Style Drifts: Benchmarking Authorship Verification under Distribution Shifts in Genre, Time and the AI-Era

evidence: Section 1 (Contributions): 'AVShift, the first German benchmark comprising more than 150,000 text pairs for evaluating AV under cross-genre, temporal, and AI-era distribution shifts' — establishes the benchmark novelty claim.

Section 4 (AV Models): LLM approach 'fine-tunes instruction-tuned LLMs with LoRA (Hu et al., 2022)' using Gemma-4-31B-it, following the framework of Kiefer et al. (2026) — LLM use is derivative of prior work, not a methodological contribution.

Section 5 (GenreShift): 'fine-tuned LLMs perform particularly well... Mixed Gemma model achieves the strongest performance on all remaining datasets' with up to 0.77 F1 on Review-Forum; significance assessed via paired bootstrap with 10,000 resamples.

Section 4 (GenreShift Evaluation): standardized datasets normalize every document to 500 words and downsample to 3,640 samples — a genuine confound control; Appendix E shows Gemma is no longer consistently superior under these controls, an honestly reported negative result.

Section 5 (TimeShift): 'F1-score dropping from 0.90 for text pairs separated by 0–12 months to 0.69 after 9–10 years' with significant negative Pearson/Spearman correlations — supports the temporal-drift claim quantitatively.

Section 5 (AIShift) and Limitations: 'no evidence that the emergence of genAI has introduced a systematic distribution shift', explicitly caveated because 'our corpus was not annotated for AI-assisted writing' — claim strength appropriately matched to evidence.

Section 5 (CrossNews): Gemma improves on Ma et al. (2025) by 0.11 F1 (Tweet-Tweet) and 0.07 (Article-Tweet) — partial cross-lingual validation, though the paper notes benchmark differences 'prevent attribution of the performance gap to language alone'.
Limitations: evaluation covers 'a representative but limited selection of AV approaches' and AVShift is built from 'a single German platform' — generalizability constraints are self-acknowledged.

Appendix C and Appendix I: four H200 GPUs, LoRA hyperparameters following Kiefer et al. (2026), dataset released pseudonymized for research use, code/scraping pipeline released — strong reproducibility provisions, though dataset availability is stated in future tense.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An in-scope NLP/LLM evaluation paper: it introduces AVShift, the first German authorship-verification benchmark spanning cross-genre, temporal, and AI-era distribution shifts (150k+ pairs, Section 3), and benchmarks feature-based (XGBoost), embedding-based (MSR), and LLM-based (LoRA fine-tuned Gemma-4-31B-it) approaches. LLM relevance is substantive but instrumental: the LLM is one of three paradigms evaluated and the paper follows an existing fine-tuning framework (Kiefer et al., 2026) rather than contributing LLM methodology. Novelty is solid for a benchmark (unified multi-shift German setting, feature stability score, underexplored temporal shift), but methods are borrowed. Rigor is a strength: standardized datasets controlling text length and training size (Section 4, 500-word normalization, 3,640-sample downsampling), paired bootstrap significance testing (10,000 resamples), leave-one-era-out AI-shift protocol, and honest null result on AI-era shift with acknowledged lack of AI-usage annotation (Section 5, Limitations). Evidence is quantitative and mostly well supported (F1 0.89/0.80/0.78 per genre; Review TimeShift drop 0.90→0.69; CrossNews gains of 0.11/0.07 F1 over Ma et al. 2025), though only one model per paradigm and exact correlation values are relegated to figures. Generalizability is limited by a single German platform (fanfiktion.de), partially mitigated by the English CrossNews validation. Reproducibility claims are good: dataset release with pseudonymization, code, full environment/hyperparameters in Appendix C, licenses in Appendix I.

primary_link.title: When Writing Style Drifts: Benchmarking Authorship Verification under Distribution Shifts in Genre, Time and the AI-Era

papers.summary: Authorship verification (AV) assumes that an author's writing style remains sufficiently stable to distinguish it from that of other writers. In practice, however, this assumption is challenged by distribution shifts caused by changes in genre, time, and AI-assisted writing. Existing AV benchmarks typically study these factors in isolation and focus predominantly on English, limiting our understanding of model robustness under realistic conditions. We introduce AVShift, the first German benchmar
papers.summary_zh: 作者驗證（Authorship Verification, AV）旨在判斷兩份文本是否出自同一作者，其前提是寫作風格足夠穩定；然而文體轉換、時間演進與 AI 輔助寫作皆會造成分佈偏移，挑戰此假設。既有基準多只單獨檢視單一偏移因素，且以英文為主。本文提出 AVShift，首個德文 AV 基準，涵蓋超過 15 萬個文本對，橫跨論壇貼文、評論與同人小說三種文體，以及 2004 至 2025 年共 21 年的資料，可統一評估跨文體、時間與 AI 時代三類偏移。作者比較特徵式（XGBoost 搭配 4000 餘項手工風格特徵）、嵌入（MSR）與 LLM 微調（Gemma-4-31B-it）三類方法，獲得三大發現：第一，微調後的 LLM 跨文體泛化最佳，以風格多樣的混合資料訓練可達 F1 0.77，顯示訓練資料多樣性是穩健性關鍵；第二，時間漂移是最強干擾因素，隨文本間時間間隔拉長，F1 最多下降 0.21；第三，該基準上未發現可測量的 AI 時代分佈偏移，惟資料未標註 AI 使用程度，解讀須謹慎。特徵穩定性分析顯示多數風格特徵跨文體穩定，但其重要性隨文體組合而異。限制包括評估方法選擇有限、資料僅來自單一德文平台。此研究對鑑識語言學與抄襲偵測等高風險應用的可靠評估深具意義。
papers.title: When Writing Style Drifts: Benchmarking Authorship Verification under Distribution Shifts in Genre, Time and the AI-Era
papers.title_zh: 當寫作風格漂移時：在文體、時間與 AI 時代分佈偏移下的作者驗證基準測試

links.title: Code as Representation: A Compilable Parsing Paradigm for Academic Documents

§3.5: VRF is MLLM-as-judge; Gemini-3-Pro judge achieved 86% exact agreement with humans on 100 validation samples; GPT-5.5 cross-evaluation differs <3%

Table 4: 14 models evaluated with code and visual metrics; Gemini-3-Pro best overall (Pixel Sim. 47.28); pseudocode VRF-S collapses for GPT-5.4 (13.04) and Claude Opus 4.6 (17.39)
Table 5: full multi-agent system improves over base by roughly 3-7 points; self-reflection degrades all metrics; removing visual feedback raises formula CDM from 74.20 to 75.30
§4.5: format-sensitive QA uses only 90 manually annotated questions across three formats and three models; LaTeX+Python helps Qwen3.5-Plus most
§3.3/Fig. 2: chart ground truth is generated by Gemini-3-Pro and retained only after expert visual verification, not original author code
Footnote 1: CADP-Bench released at https://github.com/AriKing11/CADP-Bench; Appendix A provides all parsing and evaluation prompts
llm_evaluation.rationale: A benchmark/evaluation paper for MLLM-based academic document parsing that reconstructs pages as LaTeX plus executable Python with a re-injection compilation protocol. It aligns well with mid-weight preferences: LLM/MLLM evaluation (14 SOTA models in Table 4), code generation as the core representation (§3.1.2), an exploratory multi-agent baseline with tools, decomposition, and feedback (§4.1.2, RQ3 ablations in Table 5), and LLM-as-judge evaluation (VRF, §3.5). It does not touch the top-weight Japanese LLM/NLP or reasoning/CoT topics, and is closer to a multimodal document-understanding benchmark than LLM methodology, capping preference relevance. Novelty is solid: full-page dual-code generation with compilability-verified reconstruction is a genuine gap versus Markdown or isolated element-code benchmarks (Table 1, §2.2). Rigor is above average: 1,630 expert-verified samples with 88% inter-annotator agreement (§3.6), judge-human agreement of 86% on 100 samples plus a cross-judge check with GPT-5.5 differing <3% (§3.5), three evaluation runs per sample (§4.1.3), and ablations including counter-productive effects of self-reflection and visual feedback. Evidence is quantitative and mostly consistent with claims, though VRF-S pseudocode scores rest on few samples (only 138 pseudocode elements, Table 3), the 90-question QA study (§4.5) is small, and there is mild circularity in using Gemini-3-Pro for chart ground truth generation, as judge, and as top model, only partially mitigated by human verification (§3.3, Fig. 2). Generalizability is moderate: multi-domain coverage but restricted to LaTeX-sourced academic pages; reproducibility is supported by the released CADP-Bench (footnote 1) and full evaluation prompts (Appendix A), though multi-agent implementation specifics are thin.

primary_link.title: Code as Representation: A Compilable Parsing Paradigm for Academic Documents

papers.summary: Academic papers are a primary carrier of scientific knowledge, yet most of this knowledge remains locked in PDFs that are optimized for human reading rather than machine use. For Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), the core challenge is not only perception, but representation: scientific pages interleave text with Structured Academic Elements (SAEs) such as tables, formulas, charts, and pseudocode, whose structure, data, and logic are poorly preserved by common surrogates like Markdown. We
papers.summary_zh: 學術論文多以 PDF 呈現，其版面為人類閱讀而設計，難以轉為機器可用的表示。常見的 Markdown 解析會造成結構塌陷、圖表淪為靜態截圖，且無法回編譯驗證。本文提出可編譯學術文件解析（CADP）典範：模型輸入整頁截圖與有限的編譯環境資訊，同時生成情境化 LaTeX 與可執行的 Python 程式碼，分別重建文字、表格、公式、虛擬碼，以及圖表背後的資料與繪圖邏輯。作者建立專家驗證的 CADP-Bench，收錄 1,630 個含至少兩類結構化學術元素的整頁樣本，並以「再注入編譯」協定評估：執行 Python 產生圖表、將生成的 LaTeX 回填原始文件後以 pdfLaTeX 編譯，再與原頁比對。指標涵蓋 CDM、TEDS、PRS、以 MLLM 為評審的 VRF 及像素相似度等。結果顯示 Gemini-3-Pro 整體最佳，但連前緣模型在虛擬碼等結構密集元素上仍劇烈崩潰；探索性多代理基線可再提升約 3 至 7 分，單純自我反思反而造成退步；格式敏感問答實驗也顯示結構保留表示能補償中等規模模型的不足。此典範為強化學習獎勵設計與 Graph-RAG 奠基，凸顯高保真可執行重建仍是重大挑戰。
papers.title: Code as Representation: A Compilable Parsing Paradigm for Academic Documents
papers.title_zh: 程式碼作為表示：學術文件的可編譯解析典範

links.title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

evidence: Abstract: 'MixerLoop surpasses FullLoop on aggregate CORE at 15M and retains 41.5% of its CORE improvement at 110M while reducing recurrent-backbone projection FLOPs by 45.9%.'

Section 3.2 Training Settings: 'matched unique parameter counts, data, processed-token budgets, optimization settings... 100,000 streamed updates (52.43B processed tokens/model), and global batch 512... no architecture-specific hyperparameter search.'
Section 4.2: 'At 15M, MixerLoop reaches CORE 6.52, above NoLoop's 5.01 and FullLoop's 5.52... At 110M, MixerLoop raises CORE from 14.16 to 15.56, while FullLoop reaches 17.52.'
Section 4.1 Evaluation: 'The reported results correspond to one final checkpoint per architecture' — no seed variance or error bars reported.
Section 2 Related Work: 'SGT... identifies high-entropy softmax attention heads, repeats them, and applies the FFN once' — close precedent limiting architectural novelty.
Section 3.4 / Eq. 16-19: Iterative Transport Rank defined as participation-ratio rank of Hellinger-space intervention trajectory; marginal ITR measures nonredundant readout updates.
Section 4.5 Controls: randomly initialized 15M control has ITR 1.068 with Hellinger effect 6.4e-6 and -1.5e-4 nats target change; stability across resampled windows and 128->256 token contexts.
Section 4.3 Inference Efficiency: 1.34x throughput at 15M batch 32 and 1.52x at 110M batch 16 (RTX 3090 Ti, BF16 prefill, length 1024).
Section 5 Discussion: 'Whether this hierarchy holds for softmax attention, other linear mixers, sparse FFNs, and larger scales remains open.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM architecture research: operator-selective recurrence for looped language models using a Gated DeltaNet (linear attention/SSM) mixer, targeting latent reasoning and test-time compute efficiency. Strengths: carefully matched budgets (same unique params, 52.43B tokens, data order, optimizer, no per-architecture tuning, Sec 3.2), honest reporting (FullLoop beats MixerLoop at 110M, Sec 4.2), a genuinely novel diagnostic (ITR/marginal ITR via finite context-off interventions measured at the LM readout, Sec 3.4), and good controls (random-init intervention control, resampled windows, context-length stability checks, Sec 4.5). Weaknesses: only two baselines (no head-to-head with SGT, the closest prior that already loops attention heads with the FFN applied once, Sec 2), a single seed and single final checkpoint per architecture with no variance estimates (Sec 4.1) at small 15M/110M scale where chance-adjusted CORE gaps (~1.5 points) may be fragile, and the mixer-vs-FFN allocation claim is demonstrated only for one mixer at T=4. Generalizability is limited by the authors' own admission (Sec 5). Training details are thorough but no code/checkpoint release is stated. Overall: solid, honest, moderately novel empirical study with a useful new measurement tool, but not decisive evidence at scale.
topics: Linear attention / state space models (Gated DeltaNet)

primary_link.title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

papers.summary: Looped language models improve reasoning and knowledge manipulation by applying shared computation repeatedly. Existing systems usually repeat an entire layer stack, although a mixer and a dense feed-forward network (FFN) perform different operations and have different costs. We ask a narrower question: what should loop? We view recurrence as repeated composition of a state update and argue that an application is valuable when it exposes a new cross-position influence direction that remains obse
papers.summary_zh: 迴圈語言模型透過重複使用共享參數來增加運算深度，但現有系統多半重複整個 Transformer 區塊，未回答「什麼元件值得迴圈」。本文聚焦 Gated DeltaNet 混合器與密集前饋網路（FFN）的成本與功能差異，提出 MixerLoop：每層僅重複套用有狀態的 GDN 混合器，密集 FFN 只執行一次。作者以有限「關閉上下文」介入設計 Iterative Transport Rank（ITR）與邊際 ITR，量化後續混合器應用是否在最終預測讀出上產生相異、顯著且有幫助的變化。在相同參數、資料與訓練預算下比較 15M 與 110M 模型：15M 時 MixerLoop 的 CORE 平均 6.52 超越 FullLoop 的 5.52；110M 時保留 FullLoop 進步幅度的 41.5%，卻將遞迴主幹投影 FLOPs 減少 45.9%，預填充吞吐量最高達 1.52 倍。介入分析顯示後續混合器步驟持續產生非冗餘、且對正確下一詞有正向貢獻的讀出更新，隨機初始化對照組則無此現象。限制方面，110M 規模下 FullLoop 在聚合能力仍較強，且此層級關係是否適用於其他混合器與更大規模尚待驗證。此研究指出遞迴深度應優先配置給有狀態的混合器，重複執行 FFN 並非必要。
papers.title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

links.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence

evidence: Abstract: 'ASI-Bench contains 60 project-level research tasks across 11 scientific domains and progressively reduces methodological guidance'; '18 state-of-the-art agent-model configurations, the average score drops from 50.91 with full methodological guidance to 29.10 ... and 26.62 when agents must determine the method themselves'.
Section 3.1, Table 2: per-configuration B1-B4 scores with one-sample std over three independent runs; footnote states Claude Opus 5 result 'obtained from a single run'.

Section 2.2 'Rigorous Construction and Validation': 'five review rounds, more than 1,100 review assignments, and over 2,000 task revisions' and 'more than 1,500 sandbox runs'; claims 31,000+ human-hours.

Section 3.1 'Harnesses Shape Model's Capability': MiMo V2.5 Pro improves 'from 16.17 with MiMo Code to 23.25 with Claude Code' and Kimi K2.7 'rises from 19.72 with Kimi Code to 27.34 with Claude Code'.

Section 3.2, Figure 4: 'B2 is the most expensive setting, requiring 6.91M tokens and 49.7 minutes per task-59% more tokens and 32% more time than B1'; cost-performance figures quoted (~$684 vs ~$2,728 per run).

Appendix A 'Scientific Autonomy and Guidance Dependence': 'none evaluates how agents transition from following a prescribed method to independently constructing and validating a workflow within the same scientific project'; acknowledges ScienceAgentBench, ProjectionBench, ProjectEval as closest prior designs.
Appendix D Case Study: full B1-B4 prompt examples for a 2D anisotropic stiff PDE task, showing the guidance gradient concretely (B1 gives PDE, ETDRK4 coefficients; B3 gives data and objective only).

Appendix C: contribution process requires 'four prompt variants, B1-B4', 'generate_gt.py', 'evaluation specification containing validity checks and weighted scoring criteria', and 'evidence from local evaluation across all four information conditions'.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-agent evaluation benchmark (ASI-Bench) that tests frontier models (GPT-5.x, Claude, Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax, MiMo) under agent harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, OpenHands, etc.) on autonomous scientific research, squarely matching high-weight preferences (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, Reasoning, Evaluation). Core design contribution is the B1-B4 guidance-withdrawal gradient within matched project instances, which is a real but incremental novelty over ScienceAgentBench's binary knowledge ablation and ProjectionBench's progressive disclosure, as the paper itself concedes in Appendix A. Rigor is above average for a benchmark paper (multi-round human review, AI auditing, 1,500+ sandbox validation runs, three seeds with std devs), but weak points exist: no significance testing, no human-expert baseline, one configuration (Claude Opus 5) is single-run, per-domain task counts are small (~5.5/domain over 60 tasks), and scoring rubric details/inter-rater agreement are not shown. Main quantitative claims (B1 50.91 -> B2 29.10 -> B3 26.62 mean drop) are large relative to reported noise and replicated across 18 configurations, supporting the headline conclusion that procedural operationalization, not method selection, is the bottleneck; but B4-vs-B3 differences (~+0.36 mean) are within reported stds, so the distractor-robustness conclusion is weakly supported. Reproducibility claims are concrete (public portal, GitHub/HuggingFace/leaderboard links, generate_gt.py requirements, guided contribution flow) though not verifiable from the text alone. Not a narrow domain application; in scope.

primary_link.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence

papers.summary: Artificial superintelligence (ASI) requires AI to move beyond mastering existing knowledge toward exploring the unknown, creating new knowledge, and turning new ideas into verifiable results. However, the capabilities of today's AI systems are still largely built on learning, compressing, and applying existing human knowledge. Accordingly, existing benchmarks primarily test whether AI can produce correct answers based on learned knowledge, or whether it can complete tasks under extensive human g
papers.summary_zh: 人工超級智慧（ASI）要求 AI 超越學習既有知識，能探索未知、創造新知並產出可驗證的成果。然而現有基準多測試已知答案的問題，或讓 AI 在人類詳細指導下完成任務。本文提出 ASI-Bench，首個跨領域同時評估「創新探索」與「自主科學執行」的專案級基準，並在同一研究專案內逐步撤除人類方法學指導。基準由逾 40 位專家投入超過 31,000 小時打造，涵蓋 11 個科學領域共 60 個專案級任務，經五輪人工審查、AI 輔助稽核與沙盒端到端執行驗證。評測採四級指導梯度：B1 給予完整方法步驟、B2 僅給方法名稱、B3 只給研究目標與資料、B4 再加入干擾資訊。在 18 組最先進代理與模型組合上，平均分數由 B1 的 50.91 驟降至 B2 的 29.10 與 B3 的 26.62，顯示主要瓶頸在於將方法轉化為完整可執行程序，而非選擇方法本身；B4 分數與 B3 相近，顯示干擾資訊影響有限。最強組合 Codex 搭配 GPT-5.6 Sol ultra 的 B3 也僅 51.60 分，且代理框架（harness）顯著影響同一模型的表现。基準遠未飽和並開放社群擴充，可作為追蹤自主科學研究能力的公共基礎設施。
papers.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence
papers.title_zh: ASI-Bench：邁向人工超級智慧的黎明

links.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference

evidence: §4.1 Baselines: frozen backbone is Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; ICL and RAG (128-token chunks, BGE-Large embeddings, K∈{1,4,8}) are the only baselines evaluated at 4K–128K.
Table 1: MoNe reports 0.96/0.94/0.96 on S-NIAH/MK-NIAH/FWE at 128K while ICL falls to 0.28/0.00/0.23 beyond the native 32K window and RAG plateaus (0.89/0.71/0.60).
Table 2: at 128K, MoNe totals 1.41 GB peak GPU memory and 149.61T FLOPs vs ICL's 7.07 GB and 786.33T FLOPs (↓80%/↓81%), supporting the abstract's 80% claim.

§4.4 Figure 4: layer ablation shows all-24-layer attachment at 1.00/0.98/0.94 (4K/64K/128K) vs last-8 collapse to 0.15/0.02 (64K/128K); segment size T=512 (0.98/0.94 at 64K/128K) beats T=128 (0.85/0.53).

§3.2–3.3: SwiGLU memory module and associative memory loss are stated as 'Following Zhang et al. (2026)' (LaCT), with the paper's additions being memory-token KV injection into frozen attention and segment-local RoPE.

Limitations section: validation is restricted to a Qwen2.5-0.5B backbone and controlled RULER retrieval tasks; larger scales and naturalistic long-document/conversational workloads are deferred to future work.

Appendix A.1–A.2: 30K training samples per N∈{2..8} (1K–4K), 100 eval samples per length; LoRA rank 128, AdamW (0.9/0.95), lr 1e-3/5e-5, bf16 — detailed enough for partial reproduction, but no code or artifact release is mentioned.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM long-context methodology paper, strongly aligned with LLM, long-context/memory, transformer-attention, and inference-efficiency preferences. It attaches a test-time-trained fast-weight memory to a frozen Transformer (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), reporting strong RULER results and ~80% FLOPs/memory reduction at 128K. Main weaknesses: the memory mechanism and loss are explicitly 'Following Zhang et al. (2026)' (LaCT), so novelty is mostly the plug-in KV injection and segment-local RoPE; evaluation uses only one small backbone and three synthetic RULER tasks, with ICL as a partially strawman baseline beyond the native window and no comparison to other context-compression or TTT-adapted methods; no seeds/variance; no code release. Length generalization (4K training to 128K eval) is a genuine strength, but generalization across model scales and task types is unverified and acknowledged in Limitations.

primary_link.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference

papers.summary: We present MoNe, a lightweight modular neural memory that attaches to any frozen pretrained Transformer to enable long-context inference without retraining. MoNe reads context in fixed-size segments via test-time learning of fast-weight neural memory networks with layer-localized gradient updates; at inference, the memory generates keys and values from the query tokens alone, with no context tokens re-read. This two-phase design decouples inference cost from context length, achieving $O(N)$ prep
papers.summary_zh: 長上下文推論是 LLM 應用的關鍵瓶頸：in-context learning 的注意力運算隨長度呈平方成長，KV cache 也隨之膨脹；RAG 僅能處理局部可復原的事實，難以整合散落全文的多重線索；遞迴架構則需從頭重新訓練。本文提出 MoNe，一種可附加於任何凍結預訓練 Transformer 的輕量模組化神經記憶，無須修改主幹權重。其採兩階段設計：測試時學習階段以 512 token 分段依序讀入上下文，透過層級局部化的梯度更新訓練各層 SwiGLU 快速權重神經記憶，以結合記憶損失將鍵值關聯寫入記憶；推論階段僅由查詢 token 讀取記憶，生成固定的記憶 token 注入注意力機制，不再直接存取原始上下文。因此預處理為 O(N)、查詢為 O(1)，GPU 記憶體占用與上下文長度無關。在 128K token 時，相較 ICL 總運算與峰值記憶體各減少約 80%，參數開銷僅 6.4%。模型僅以 4K 以內上下文訓練，即能外推至 128K（32 倍），在 RULER 的 S-NIAH、MK-NIAH 與高頻詞抽取任務上維持接近滿分，而 ICL 超出原生 32K 視窗後劇烈崩潰。消融實驗顯示覆蓋全部層與較大分段尺寸為最佳取捨。目前驗證局限於 0.5B 主幹與受控檢索任務，未來可延伸至更大規模與真實文件工作負載。

links.title: SESSE: Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate -- LLM-as-Judge Evaluation via Structured Decomposition

evidence: Abstract: 'On RewardBench (n=1,000), SESSE achieves near-parity with the chain-of-thought baseline and is competitive with RISE-Judge-32B (92.7%)... while remaining fully training-free.'

Section 3.1: RewardBench 2,985 pairwise examples, dev n=1,985 / val n=1,000 random split; judges are Qwen2-VL-7B, Gemini Flash Lite, Gemini 2.5 Flash; k=25 clusters by silhouette analysis, temperature 0.
Table 1: Gemini 2.5 Flash SESSE non-tie 0.933 vs holistic 0.945 (p>0.05 McNemar); Flash Lite (0.820 vs 0.880) and Qwen2-VL-7B (0.663 vs 0.698) gaps significant at p<0.05; tie rates 21.3%/2.6%/3.5%.

Section 4 (Discussion): 'CoT holistic itself already outperforms RISE-Judge, so SESSE's comparable accuracy mainly shows that it preserves the base model's advantage without requiring fine-tuning' — an honest tempering of the specialist-parity claim.

Section 4 (Domain-specific signal recovery): donotanswer subset gains +20.6% relative (75.9%→91.5%); xstest-should-respond drops 27.1% relative due to Tier-1 false positives on borderline-safe prompts.

Appendix A Table A.1: depth sweep n=1–10 shows saturation (Gemini ~0.92–0.933); Qwen2-VL-7B peaks at n=3 (0.663) then degrades from redundant sub-questions (51.9% of instances covered by one dominant protasis).
Appendix B Table B.1: cross-model bank transfer (Gemini bank with Qwen judge) peaks at same 66.3%, attributing ceiling to judge capability not bank quality.

Limitations: bank portability requires re-running Stages 0–4 per judge/domain; k=25 fixed without ablation; generalization beyond RewardBench deferred; ~282 LLM calls per example at n=10; A/B/NA cannot capture end-to-end code/reasoning execution.

Section 4/Appendix C Table C.1: degradation taxonomy for configs >80% accuracy — Flash Lite 49% ambiguous/26% decomposition/26% semantic equivalence; Gemini 2.5 Flash 48% semantic equivalence (cosine 0.75 vs 0.69 dataset mean), framed as dataset property rather than model failure.

Reproducibility gaps: no code release statement, Stage-2 embedding model unnamed, only partial prompt templates given; all models (Gemini API, Qwen2-VL-7B) and RewardBench are publicly available per Section 3.1 and Ethical Considerations.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-methodology paper: training-free LLM-as-judge evaluation via structured decomposition, directly matching LLM, evaluation/benchmark, reasoning-decomposition, and interpretability preferences. The error-driven criterion mining (no oracle responses or fine-tuning) is a genuine, if incremental, advance over G-Eval/Prometheus (manual rubrics) and CheckEval/DeCE (oracle-derived). Rigor is above average: three judges, McNemar tests, depth ablation (Appendix A), cross-model bank transfer (Appendix B), and an honest failure taxonomy (Appendix C) that concedes the headline comparison is weaker than it sounds — CoT holistic (94.5%) already beats RISE-Judge (92.7%), so SESSE mainly preserves base-model accuracy. Quantitative evidence is concrete (Table 1, subset shifts like donotanswer 75.9%→91.5% and xstest −27.1% relative), but the claim of 'parity with a fine-tuned specialist' is somewhat inflated and rests on one model. Strong deductions for scope: single benchmark (RewardBench only), no open-ended/multi-turn/non-English evaluation, bank not portable across judges or domains, k=25 unexplored, ~282 LLM calls per example overhead, and no code/prompt-artifact release or full specification (embedding model for clustering unnamed), limiting reproducibility.

primary_link.title: SESSE: Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate -- LLM-as-Judge Evaluation via Structured Decomposition

papers.summary: LLM-as-judge evaluation reduces response quality assessment to a single holistic A/B preference choice, providing no mechanism to isolate which quality dimensions drove the preference or distinguish model errors from genuine label ambiguity. We propose SESSE (Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate), a training-free framework that decomposes holistic judgment into structured sub-questions mined directly from the judge's own error cases; requiring no oracle responses, task-specific rubrics, or
papers.summary_zh: LLM-as-Judge 評估通常將回應品質化約為單一整體的 A/B 偏好選擇，無法分辨是哪些品質面向驅動了判斷，也難以區分評審錯誤與真實的標註模糊。本文提出 SESSE，一個免訓練的五階段架構：先在開發集上收集評審出錯的案例，據此自動生成「若條件成立，A 或 B 何者較符合某屬性，或 NA（不適用）」的條件式子問題；再將候選子問題嵌入、聚類成 k 組，以 greedy farthest-first traversal 排序，為每組生成摘要式描述並合併重複群組；推論時先挑選相關群組，再逐一以 A/B/NA 投票，最終偏好由 A/B 票的多數決定。在 RewardBench 驗證集（n=1,000）上，SESSE 搭配 Gemini 2.5 Flash 達 93.3% 準確率、平手率僅 3.5%，與經 SFT+DPO 微調的專家評審 RISE-Judge 32B（92.7%）同級，且與 CoT 整體基準的差距不顯著；但較弱的 Flash Lite 與 Qwen2-VL-7B 仍呈現統計顯著落差，且各模型在平手案例上的整體準確率都明顯較低，顯示平手標記著真正的標註模糊。限制包括：問題庫綁定特定評審與開發集，更換模型或領域需重跑離線流程；n=10 時每例約需 282 次 LLM 呼叫；A/B/NA 子問題無法處理端對端執行驗證，且實驗僅限 RewardBench。其價值在於逐準則投票提供可稽核的證據軌跡，能診斷標註雜訊與評審失敗模式，平手率更可作為不需標籤的評審可靠度訊號。
papers.title: SESSE: Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate -- LLM-as-Judge Evaluation via Structured Decomposition
papers.title_zh: SESSE：草擬、擴充、排序、摘要、評估——以結構化分解進行 LLM-as-Judge 評估

links.title: Preference Is Not Intervention: The Structure and Stability Boundaries of Reader-Specific Evidence Utility

evidence: Abstract and §5.1: reader×query interaction explains 29.8% of utility variance vs 8.4% permutation-null median (p<10^-4); readers disagree on effect sign in 33.3% of dual-nonzero cells (1,067/3,206; bootstrap CI [0.283, 0.377])

§5.2 and Table 5: ordinal geometry stable across four independent settings (LOO 0.599 [0.370, 0.764]; PRISM 0.786; RAMDocs 0.833; RAGuard 0.685), with PRISM identity-shuffle null 0.314 vs observed 0.786 (Appendix E)

§5.3 and Table 1: conditional signed geometry far below sparsity-matched nulls in open-ended QA (LOO 0.138 vs null 0.363, p=2×10^-4; RAMDocs 0.345 vs 0.376), but strong in binary fact-checking (RAGuard 0.748 vs ordinal 0.685)
§5.4 and Table 6: open-QA signed instability localizes to misleading (0.104) and noise (0.093) evidence; RAGuard shows 0.658/0.713/0.377 across positions
§5.6 and Appendix H: transfer experiment (4,050 cells) shows oracle-distance vs regret ρ=-0.271 (p=0.264), regret split-half reliability -0.281 [-0.530, 0.001]; frozen decision rule not met
Appendix F: accidental duplicate run gives test-retest flip rate f=0.123, capping attenuation-corrected signed reliability at 0.242, below ordinal 0.599
Ethics and Reproducibility section: 'artifacts, frozen plans, and analysis scripts will be released' — release promised but not yet available; Appendix J maps claims to frozen artifact filenames
§8 Limitations: task boundary causal axis not identified; forced-choice perturbation partial evidence with label-stratum degeneracy (Appendix G: gold=B stratum degenerate)
llm_evaluation.rationale: A controlled measurement study of reader-specific evidence utility in RAG, squarely within LLM/RAG scope: 9-13 LLM endpoints (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, GPT-5.6, Llama, Ministral) are the objects of study, with retrieval personalization per generator as the motivating application. Methodological novelty is moderate: concurrent work [14] already proposed LLM-specific passage utility and limited transfer; this paper's contribution is the controlled decomposition into activity/ordinal/conditional-signed geometry with stability calibration. Rigor is a clear strength: split-half reliability over 1,000 stratified splits, sparsity-matched permutation nulls, PRISM identity/order/size-matched artifact controls, test-retest attenuation bounds on decoding noise (Appendix F), a transparent alternative-explanations table (Table 2), frozen pre-registered decision rules, and honest reporting of negative results (transfer gate not met, behavior probe bank saturated in Appendix I). Evidence is strong for the headline ordinal-stable/signed-weak claims but some estimates rest on small samples: internal signed 0.138 with CI [-0.077, 0.356] over 3,206 dual-nonzero cells, transfer underpowered (mean regret 0.035 vs SE 0.037, Appendix H), and the forced-choice mechanism is explicitly only suggestive. Generalizability is limited by QA-centric tasks, token-F1 metrics, English-only data, and two external arms using different reader panels. Reproducibility is well-documented (prompt contracts, seeds, artifact map in Appendix J) but artifacts are only promised ('will be released'), not yet available. Not a pure domain application; no scope exclusion applies.

primary_link.title: Preference Is Not Intervention: The Structure and Stability Boundaries of Reader-Specific Evidence Utility

papers.summary: ML systems increasingly condition decisions on downstream model identity, but this is useful only if model-specific differences form reusable structure rather than input-local interactions. We test this in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), where evidence utility can be measured under controlled interventions. Holding query, evidence, task, scoring, and intervention fixed, nine readers disagree on effect sign in 33\% of jointly affected cells; reader$\times$query interaction explains 29.8\% o
papers.summary_zh: RAG 系統日益依賴下游模型身分來挑選證據，但唯有當模型間差異構成可重用結構、而非輸入局部的互動時，這種個人化才有意義。本文在高度控制的設定下提問：固定查詢、證據、任務與介入方式，僅改變讀者（模型）身分，是否會產生可重現的證據效用差異，以及哪些成分能跨查詢保持穩定。作者讓 9 個讀者在 100 個 NQ/HotpotQA 查詢上進行 leave-one-out 介入以建構效用張量，區分活動性、序數偏好與條件性正負方向（幫助或傷害）三個物件，再以 split-half 信度搭配稀疏度匹配的置換虛無，於四個獨立設定（內部 LOO、PRISM 偏好資料、RAMDocs、RAGuard）檢驗穩定性。結果顯示讀者專屬效用確實存在：讀者×查詢互動解釋 29.8% 變異（虛無中位數 8.4%），33% 的雙非零格子符號相反，自選證據 F1 提升 +0.031；序數幾何在四個設定皆穩定（ρ=0.60–0.83），但正負方向幾何在開放式問答近乎失穩（0.14、0.35），弱點集中在誤導與無關證據，於二元事實查核中則強勁穩定（0.75）。跨讀者轉移實驗更顯示，穩定的序數相似度無法預測介入轉移的 regret（ρ=-0.27，不顯著）。限制包括：任務邊界的因果軸尚未確立、強制選擇探針僅屬暗示性證據、各實驗臂的讀者群不同。核心訊息是「偏好並非介入」：排序與組成可依讀者個人化，但幫助/傷害方向在開放式問答中應視為查詢局部屬性。
papers.title: Preference Is Not Intervention: The Structure and Stability Boundaries of Reader-Specific Evidence Utility
papers.title_zh: 偏好並非介入：讀者專屬證據效用的結構與穩定性邊界

links.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance

evidence: §6.4 Methodology: 'The Prompt-Only agent uses a regex-based MockLLM; no live LLM API calls are made in this deterministic suite' and 'the suite validates the verifier's decision logic rather than robustness to unmodelled DeFi behavior'.
§7.1 Table 1 (2,800 trials, 10 seeds): PACE 100.0% correct, 0.00 unsafe execution, 0.00 FP; strongest baseline SimGuard 0.0312 attack success, missing only the calldata-mutation task.

§7.3 Table 2 (320 ablation trials, seed 42): permissive policy raises unsafe rate 0.000→0.575 (+57.5pp); removing touched-contract allowlist gives 0.125 (+12.5pp); removing calldata binding or freshness gives 0.025 each.

§7.5 Table 3 (595 live trials, 3 OpenAI-compatible models): PACE-guarded attack success 0.000 for all models while unguarded gpt-4o judged 11/160 attacks safe; benign FP 5.0–12.8% attributed to model/parser variance.
§7.7 Table 4: PACE blocks 8/8 policy-aware evasion attacks but admits 8/8 policy-valid-but-harmful transactions 'by design', delineating soundness vs. completeness.
§7.6 Mainnet-Fork Execution Harness: results 'reported only when the corresponding artifacts are generated'; no fork results are presented in the paper.
§7.4: measured PDR overhead 29,826–31,822 gas (~91.7% relative for an approval, ~50.5% for a swap), with 21 Foundry tests described in §5.6.

Scope statement (§1) and §4.6: claims framed as 'logic-level safety within a reproducible benchmark rather than deployment-ready DeFi security'; soundness requires reconstructing semantic fields 'from decoded calldata and the simulation trace using trusted code'.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strong match to high-weight preferences: the paper is centrally about LLM-agent safety (Agents & Tool Use w2.5, AI Safety w2.0, LLM w2.5) with prompt-injection defense, an attack benchmark, and a live three-model LLM evaluation. It is not a pure domain application since the language-model/agent methodology is the core contribution. Novelty is moderate: the PDR construction that cryptographically binds an off-chain verifier decision plus simulation to exact calldata bytes, re-checked on-chain, is a concrete step beyond existing smart-account guards (which the related-work section admits 'validate over on-chain state alone'), but the components (allowlists, value caps, slippage bounds, simulation) are standard. Rigor is mixed: the headline 0.00 unsafe rate comes from a deterministic sandbox where the 'LLM' is a regex mock and tasks are, by the authors' own admission, 'constructed around the policy's modeled properties' (§6.4), making the main result close to a logic-level self-check; however, ablations (§7.3), an adaptive-adversary study (§7.7), gas measurements (§7.4), and an honest live-LLM suite with 5.0–12.8% false positives (§7.5) strengthen the evaluation. The mainnet-fork harness yields no reported results (§7.6), and the repository is only 'open-sourced upon acceptance'. Generalizability is limited by DeFi-specific checks, the trusted-reconstruction assumption for typed fields (§4.6), and admission that all guards accept policy-valid-but-harmful multi-step actions (§7.7).

primary_link.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance

radar.summary: Autonomous AI agents are emerging as interfaces for decentralized finance (DeFi) actions such as swaps, lending operations, and yield management. Because these agents rely on large language models (LLMs) to plan transactions, they inherit the LLM's susceptibility to prompt injection and lack of mechanisms to bind a verifier's approval to the exact transaction ultimately submitted on-chain. We present PACE (Policy-Attested Contract Execution), a transaction-level authorization framework that inte
radar.summary_zh: 以 LLM 為核心的 AI 代理正成為去中心化金融（DeFi）的操作介面，但它們繼承了 LLM 易受提示注入攻擊的弱點，且缺乏將驗證者的核准綁定到最終鏈上交易位元組的機制。本文提出 PACE，在 LLM 代理與鏈上執行之間插入三層防護：型別化的交易意圖、從不諮詢 LLM 的確定性政策驗證器，以及簽署的 Policy Decision Record（PDR），以密碼學方式將核准的意圖、政策與模擬報告綁定到確切的執行位元組，再由 Solidity 智慧帳戶在鏈上重新檢查簽章、calldata 雜湊、nonce 與有效期。在涵蓋四類攻擊與良性任務的 40 項基準、六個非 PACE 基線、共 2,800 次試驗的確定性沙盒中，PACE 達到 0.00 的不安全執行率與 0.00 的誤報率，未防護基線則高達 0.80；消融實驗指出寬鬆政策設定（+57.5 個百分點）與被觸及合約允許清單（+12.5 個百分點）是安全主因；鏈上 gas 開銷為 29,826–31,822。三個真實模型的線上評估中，防護後攻擊成功率皆為 0；面對完全知曉政策的自適應對手可阻擋全部 8 項規避攻擊，但政策允許卻有害的交易仍全數放行，這是設計上明示的保證邊界。限制：實驗採用 regex 模擬 LLM 與記憶體內模擬器，僅主張邏輯層級的安全，且未涵蓋金鑰外洩、多步攻擊鏈或未建模的鏈上行為。其貢獻在於將代理安全與模型可信度解耦，確立交易層級政策認證的可行性。
radar.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance
radar.title_zh: PACE：政策認證合約執行——保障去中心化金融中 AI 代理的安全

links.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

evidence: Abstract: method applied to 119,147 decisions by 78,657 subjects across 10 game roles; behavior matched with three dimensions (Risk Aversion, Strategic Sophistication, Trust) that cluster into fewer than a dozen groups.
Section 3.2 / Appendix A.1: prompts insert type vectors like 'Altruism: 2 out of 5' as system prompts paired with game instructions; main model is GPT-4.1 with exact prompt templates given.
Section 5.1 / Figure 5: median individual matching error falls from 0.288 (default prompt) to 0.132 with one dimension, flattening after three dimensions.
Section 5.3 / Figure 7: best type-based held-out prediction error is 1.11x the HistGBT benchmark (vs 1.43 for a random human draw and 1.73 for uniform), ranging 0.94-1.24 across games.
Appendix C / Figure A1: one-dimensional effects replicate across gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro with correlation-of-correlations r=0.83-0.88 vs GPT-4.1.
Section 6 / Figure 8: economic keywords outperform Big-5 and placebo keywords from two through five dimensions, with placebo benefit quickly diminishing.
Footnote 2 (Section 5.3): authors explicitly disclaim that held-out games are absent from the LLM's training corpus, limiting the strength of the out-of-distribution claim.
Appendix A.3 / Table A1: full data provenance including snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, 777,696 main-analysis responses, collection dates, and extraction pipeline (4.3% fallback adjudication).
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-methodology paper whose core contribution is a structured prompting scheme (type-vector system prompts over Likert-scale behavioral dimensions) used to measure the dimensionality of human behavior across ten economic game roles. It squarely matches LLM (weight 2.5) and prompting/in-context (1.5) preferences, and is not a pure domain application since the prompting/portability method itself is the contribution. Rigor is above average: 119,147 human decisions from 78,657 subjects, distribution and individual-level fitting, placebo and Big-5 keyword controls, a HistGBT benchmark with five-fold CV, and cross-model robustness over five LLMs (correlation-of-correlations r=0.83-0.88, Appendix C/Figure A1). Novelty is moderate: it refines Xie et al. (2025)-style LLM social simulation with a vectorized persona prompt rather than introducing a fundamentally new technique. Evidence is solid within scope (median individual error 0.288 default to 0.132 one-dim, Section 5.1; held-out error 1.11x HistGBT vs 1.43 random human, Section 5.3/Figure 7), though the LLM-as-measurement validity remains partially circular and the authors concede in footnote 2 that no training-data-free out-of-distribution claim is made. Generalizability is limited by a single platform (MobLab classroom students) and one game family, and reproducibility is good on prompts/model snapshots (gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, Table A1) but the human data is proprietary and no code release is stated.

primary_link.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

radar.summary: We introduce a general, easy-to-implement AI-based method for studying the structure and complexity of human behavior. We assign a large language model a ``type vector'' and then prompt it to choose actions across settings in which we observe human choices. For instance, the type vector (2,4) becomes ``You are a player characterized by the following profile: 2 out of 5 in Altruism, 4 out of 5 in Risk Aversion,'' after which it is prompted to make choices. We vary the dimensions (e.g., Altruism,
radar.summary_zh: 人類行為究竟需要多少維度才能描述？本文提出一個簡單通用的 AI 方法：為 LLM 指定一個「類型向量」（例如利他 2/5、風險趨避 4/5）作為系統提示，要求它在各種賽局情境中做出選擇，並調整維度與強度數值以貼近人類行為。作者以五個行為經濟學關鍵詞——利他、公平、風險趨避、策略成熟度、信任——應用於十種經典賽局角色，人類資料來自 MobLab 平台 78,657 名受試者、超過 35 個國家的 119,147 筆決策。結果顯示僅需三個維度——風險趨避、策略成熟度與信任——即可緊密貼合各賽局的行為分布；為個體跨賽局配適的類型向量聚集成少於十二個群組；在留一賽局的分布外預測中，類型推論的誤差已逼近直接以該賽局資料訓練的 HistGBT 機器學習基準（加權誤差為其 1.11 倍）。經濟學關鍵詞的配適表現也優於心理學 Big 5 特質與隨機安慰劑關鍵詞。限制：LLM 是黑箱，關鍵詞未必能按字面解讀；結論只是所研究十種賽局情境的上界；類型能否遷移到更歧異的真實情境仍待檢驗。此研究的重要性在於：人類行為可用低維、可攜的表示來近似，且同一類型提示可套用於任何以自然語言描述的新情境，為行為科學發展精簡的統整理論提供實證基礎與可行工具。
radar.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

links.title: DeAR: Decentralized Agentic Reasoning via Capability Grounding and Collaborative Thought Navigation

evidence: Abstract: 'Evaluations across 9 diverse multimodal reasoning and text-based QA benchmarks indicate that DeAR consistently outperforms recent baseline methods' — establishes scope in agentic LLM reasoning.
Table 1: DeAR (Ours) MathVista ALL 59.41 vs AutoGen 59.01, AgentVerse 58.79, DyLAN 59.16; ablations DeAR (Fixed Role) 51.60, w/o Thought Map 51.68, w/o Topology Update 55.65 on MathVista.

Experimental Results, 'Comparison with Baselines': 'These margins mathematically prove our superiority stems from decentralized navigation rather than vanilla model aggregation' — unsupported causal overclaim; no significance testing anywhere in the paper.
Implementation Details: text QA agents are Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-1B-IT, Llama-3.2-3B, DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Chat with FlashRAG, E5-base-v2 retriever, top k=10, zero-shot, no task-specific fine-tuning.

Decentralized Capability Grounding section, Eq. 3: capability scores are softmax-normalized benchmark accuracies (GSM8K, MMLU, TruthfulQA) taken from technical reports/model cards, not independently measured.
Effect of Decay Factor α section / Figure 4: α=0.5 gives peak MMMU 55.58 and MathVista 59.41; α range [0.1,0.9] sensitivity analysis on 2Wiki F1.
Table 3: 62.5% of MathVista queries resolved with ≤3 activated agents, supporting the adaptive-compute claim.

Abstract/Conclusion: 'The source code will be available at https://open_upon_acceptance' — placeholder availability claim; prompt templates and alignment protocols only 'provided in Appendix', so methods cannot be fully re-implemented from the paper.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core agentic-LLM reasoning paper squarely matching high-weight preferences (multi-agent frameworks, reasoning/CoT, LLMs, plus RAG-style text QA with a retriever). Decentralized peer-to-peer coordination with benchmark-derived capability grounding, a collaboration propensity matrix, and backtracking topology updates is a reasonable but incremental contribution, since the paper itself cites decentralized precursors (AgentNet) and the mechanisms are simple (softmax routing, decay-based edge pruning). Rigor is mixed: nine benchmarks and three ablations (Fixed Role, w/o Thought Map, w/o Topology Update) plus decay-factor and activation-frequency analyses support the claims, but there are no significance tests or variance estimates, baseline comparability is asserted rather than demonstrated (AutoGen/AgentVerse/DyLAN rows in Table 1), capability scores come from reported technical-report numbers rather than controlled measurement, and the text contains overclaims ('mathematically prove our superiority'). Evidence is self-reported tabular results without confidence intervals, and some cited venues/years look questionable, weakening reliability. Generalizability is supported by transfer from multimodal to text QA, but the design depends on a small fixed agent pool and availability of per-model benchmark scores. Reproducibility is weak: the code link is a placeholder ('https://open_upon_acceptance'), key hyperparameters (routing temperature T, prompts) are deferred to an unreleased appendix.

primary_link.title: DeAR: Decentralized Agentic Reasoning via Capability Grounding and Collaborative Thought Navigation

radar.summary: Existing agentic reasoning systems typically rely on centralized protocols. This design introduces routing bottlenecks and static role allocations that often fail when handling complex multimodal queries. We propose DeAR (Decentralized Agentic Reasoning), a framework that shifts from central control to autonomous peer-to-peer collaboration. DeAR is built on three mechanisms: (1) decentralized capability grounding for query-dependent agent specialization, (2) thought map navigation for targeted p
radar.summary_zh: 現有代理式推理系統多依賴集中式協定，由中央協調者負責路由與彙整，容易形成瓶頸，固定的角色分配也難以因應複雜的多模態查詢。本文提出 DeAR，改以點對點的自主協作取代中央控制，包含三項機制：(1)去中心化能力定位，讓每個代理依據可驗證的基準（如 GSM8K、MMLU、TruthfulQA）經 Softmax 正規化建立能力輪廓，並隨查詢動態調整角色；(2)思考地圖導航，以協作傾向矩陣作為動態鄰接矩陣，由當前代理在本地選擇下游同伴，逐步累積知識狀態；(3)拓撲更新，當推理路徑走進死巷時，僅對失敗的邊施加衰減因子懲罰並逐層回溯，避免整段重來。實驗涵蓋四個多模態基準（MMMU、MathVista、ChartQA、ScienceQA）與五個文字問答基準（NQ、TriviaQA、PopQA、2Wiki、HotpotQA），DeAR 在 MathVista 達 59.41、ChartQA 89.43、ScienceQA 62.45、MMMU 55.58，以四個 7B 級模型超越 Qwen2-VL-72B 等大型單模型，也勝過 AutoGen、AgentVerse、DyLAN 等集中式多代理框架。消融實驗顯示固定角色與移除拓撲更新都會明顯掉分，驗證增益來自去中心化導航而非單純的模型集成。限制包括僅在零樣本設定評估、代理池規模固定，衰減因子仍需調校。此研究顯示去中心化、能力感知的協作能避開單點瓶頸，提升知識密集推理的準確性。
radar.title: DeAR: Decentralized Agentic Reasoning via Capability Grounding and Collaborative Thought Navigation
radar.title_zh: DeAR：透過能力定位與協作式思考導航的去中心化代理推理

links.title: SGHA: Evidence-Grounded Research Problem Discovery with Local Language Models

evidence: Abstract: 'All LLM-based components of SGHA are executed using a locally served open-weight 9B language model, without requiring proprietary frontier-model APIs.'
Section 3.2: 'Our primary baseline is native AI-Scientist-v2 ideation with the same local Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B model... This is a system-level comparison rather than an information-matched ablation.'
